goal: Iske baad aap ek hi naam ke kai functions likh sakte hain, bata sakte hain ke call par compiler kaun sa chunega, aur samjha sakte hain ke kuch calls ambiguous kyun hoti hain.
warmup: Canteen mein aap kehte hain 'ek chai' to ek cup mil jata hai. Aap kehte hain 'poore group ke liye chai' to ek pot mil jata hai. Lafz 'chai' wahi hai, lekin staff dekhta hai ke aap ne kya maanga aur sahi cheez de deta hai. Overloaded functions bhi aise hi kaam karte hain. Naam wahi hota hai, jaise area, lekin compiler dekhta hai ke aap brackets ke andar kya pass kar rahe hain aur sahi version chun leta hai.
definition: Function overloading ka matlab hai ek hi NAAM ke ek se zyada functions likhna, lekin parameter lists ALAG hon. Lists parameters ki ginti, parameters ki types, ya types ke order mein alag ho sakti hain. Return type ginti mein nahi aata. Compiler version ka intikhab compile karte waqt karta hai, call ke arguments ko har parameter list se compare karke.
howItWorks: Har call ke liye compiler sab se behtar match dhoondta hai. Woh is tarteeb se pasand karta hai: (1) exact match, jahan types bilkul same hon; (2) promotion, yani ek mehfooz chhota sa widening jaise char ya bool se int; (3) conversion, jaise int se double. Agar sirf ek function sab se behtar ho to wahi use hota hai. Agar do functions barabar achhe hon to compiler ambiguity error de kar ruk jata hai, kyunke woh andaza nahi lagata. Resolver try karein: f(int) aur f(double) ke saath call f('A') f(int) use karti hai (promotion). g(int, double) aur g(double, int) ke saath call g(1, 2) ambiguous hai: har version ek argument ke liye exact match hai aur doosre ke liye conversion chahta hai. Do cheezein overload NAHI banati: sirf alag return type, ya sirf alag parameter ka naam. Default arguments ke saath ehtiyat karein: f(int a, int b = 0) aur f(int a) dono f(5) accept karte hain, jo ambiguous hai.
